source.title: LightMTP: Lightweight Latent Multi-Token Prediction
source.authors: Tamara Czinczoll; Julie Kallini; Gerard de Melo; Sha-Ni Chen

page_placements.theme: Training-induced look-ahead: objectives or data that target future tokens

record.file_problem: The text contains the full paper and appendices as provided; no clear cut-off or garbling is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses linear probes on frozen hidden states to measure future-token decodability, a different method from the cited future-token work. It does not test the rhyme-word intervention or whether a decoded feature causally changes intervening text.
record.gate_note: The directly relevant results are the linear-probe measurements of tokens several positions ahead in §5.1 and Appendix B.1/Figure 6. Other planning, reasoning, coding and benchmark outcomes concern models deliberately trained with auxiliary MTP objectives; they do not establish that unmodified next-token-prediction models spontaneously use a future-token representation to shape intervening text.
record.test_reason: The study uses linear future-token probing as a tool to evaluate models deliberately trained with auxiliary multi-token objectives. It reports only gains relative to an NTP baseline whose absolute probe accuracies are never given. So it does not measure how much future-token information arises in an ordinary hidden state. The probe gains are induced by training for that purpose and serve to compare the authors' LightMTP method with other MTP methods. No result bears on whether any version holds for ordinary models.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that LightMTP balances future-token anticipation against next-token performance better than other MTP baselines, at at most 1% extra parameters, with gains on Countdown, GSM8K format and MBPP structure. They also note, citing Future Lens, that NTP models' own look-ahead is limited and might benefit from explicit supervision; they do not measure that themselves.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains auxiliary latent-state prediction objectives and evaluates linear probe decodability. It does not reproduce the original rhyme-word representation and intervention method.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe anticipation varies with horizon: Meta-L is strongest at k = 2–5, gradually approaches other MTP methods, then falls below NTP for k ≥ 12. Variance regularization improves LightMTP anticipation but worsens some downstream language-modeling results.

fits_no_version.finding: Auxiliary MTP objectives raise linear decodability of tokens at t+k (k≥2) from final hidden states over NTP, usually at a cost at k=1. Meta-L's gain fades and falls below NTP for k≥12.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-induced look-ahead: explicit multi-token objectives increase future-token information in hidden states of small models, trading off next-token quality.

fits_no_version.finding: On Countdown, MTP-trained models keep more solution paths reachable after each equation than NTP (Figure 3). Held-out accuracy is 46.4 for NTP versus up to 58.9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MTP training improves plan-like behaviour on search tasks in small models.

record.problems: The relevant probe results are presented as plots without numerical values in the supplied text. The direct test is linear decodability, not a causal intervention on a future-token representation or a test of intervening-text changes. Most comparison models receive explicit auxiliary MTP supervision, so their probe results do not establish spontaneous look-ahead under NTP alone.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted task-performance results for Countdown, GSM8K, MBPP and general language benchmarks: these evaluate models deliberately trained with auxiliary objectives and do not measure the versions' specified internal representation-to-intermediate-text causal mechanism. Also omitted other reported probe horizons and training variants not separately described in text; Figure 6 contains plot-only curves.

untested.parts: No rhyming verse, rhyme-word representation, or intervention.
Absolute future-token decodability in an ordinary NTP model is not reported; only gains of MTP-trained models over NTP.
No test of whether NTP models pre-cache features for later positions.
No rhyme-planning analysis in open models.
Countdown look-ahead is tested only for models trained with MTP objectives; no internal look-ahead analysis of ordinary models.
No analysis of whether ordinary models' plans are shallow or incidental.

record.verdict_notes: Recommend reclassifying from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4: every probe row measures an induced effect or is the study's own method compared with others. The single spontaneous case (NTP) has no absolute value in the text. The Figure 6 caption saying all MTP models beat NTP conflicts slightly with Meta-L dipping below NTP at k≥12; both are stated in the caption.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse task, candidate rhyme-word representation, or intervention changing the line is tested.

The study probes token decodability from frozen final-layer states, but does not test whether a particular decoded feature causally shapes intervening tokens. The NTP-only baseline is shown as the reference, but the supplied text does not state its absolute probe accuracies.

The paper trains auxiliary future-state prediction objectives; it does not establish that NTP models compute features specifically because they help later positions rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction.
No rhyme-planning analysis of open-weight models using attribution-graph or probing tools is reported.
The paper evaluates Countdown, GSM8K and coding after deliberately adding MTP training objectives. It does not test spontaneous internal look-ahead in multi-step reasoning, chess or Sokoban.

The probe horizon sweep and local-structure analyses are on models with deliberately added MTP objectives; they do not establish that apparent planning in ordinary NTP models is shallow, incidental, or not used to steer generation.

relation.reason: Future-token decodability serves as a method evaluation tool; deliberately induced look-ahead does not test the claim under the supplied rules.

tranche.reason: The paper uses future-token probing to compare explicitly trained MTP objectives. It reports gains over NTP rather than absolute spontaneous future-token decodability.

source_check.notes: The qualitative method comparisons are supported, but R2–R17 should remain contextual method results rather than claim-evidence rows. Countdown's 46.4±1.4% is NTP; 58.9±1.2% is Meta-L at k=8, using held-out strict accuracy and greedy decoding.
